response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_rem FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), overall AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) AS overall_avg FROM orderexecutions), above AS (SELECT p.ordersmark, p.avg_rem, p.avg_rem - o.overall_avg AS excess_overall FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_rem > o.overall_avg), grp AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rem) AS grp_avg FROM above), kept AS (SELECT a.avg_rem, a.excess_overall, a.avg_rem - g.grp_avg AS excess_group FROM above a CROSS JOIN grp g WHERE a.avg_rem > g.grp_avg) SELECT AVG(avg_rem) AS avg_of_order_avgs, AVG(excess_overall) AS avg_excess_over_overall, AVG(excess_group) AS avg_excess_over_group FROM kept

assumptions.assumption: The overall average unfilled quantity is the mean of remaincount across all executions (nulls ignored), not the mean of the per-order averages.

The group's own average is the mean of the per-order averages for the orders above the overall average. The final three values are computed only over the orders that are also above that group average.
Executions with a NULL ordersmark form a single order group. Orders whose remaincount values are all NULL have a NULL average and drop out of the comparisons.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is the mean of the per-order averages, so each order counts equally regardless of how many executions it has.
